title: What gains AI trading can actually make - Realistic check
author: Mr_Hodlerr
selftext:
I am sharing real and honest findings. There are posts about bots and AI doing 20% in a day. That's not what I found. I ran probably one of the biggest experiments in training AI for trading and here is what my AI can really do and what it can't.

**1. Live: it matters most when the market falls.**  
This year BTC and ETH holders are down 13.8%. The same coins with AI are up 24.2%. Last week the market dropped and all 7 portfolios lost money, but every one lost less than holding.

**2. Realistic gains are 10% to 33% a year, not 20% a day.**  
The best portfolio averaged 33% a year from a typical start since 2018. That's about 2.4% a month. Anyone showing 20% a day is showing you a lucky streak, not something that holds up across years.

**3. The real edge isn't bigger gains. It's smaller losses.**  
Holding BTC and ETH since 2018 meant sitting through drops of about 75%. To get back from a 75% drop you need +300%. The AI's typical biggest drop from its high was 37%, which needs +60% to recover. This year holding fell 46.5% and needs +87% to get back. The AI's worst was 8.7%, which needs +9.5%. Losing less is what keeps your capital working.

**4. When something never recovers, AI turns out to be the better option.**  
Holding only works if the market comes back. Many coins never do. Memecoin holders since 2023 averaged -32% a year and fell as far as 89% below the money they put in. The AI on the same coins made +6.6% a year and never fell more than 26.5% below it. This year alone, memecoin holders are down 36.6% while the AI is down 6.3%. When a coin slowly bleeds toward zero, holding rides it all the way down. The AI steps aside.

**5. You choose how calm or how fast and the AI gets about 3x more return for every bit of pain.**

* Steady: about 10% a year with drops around 11%
* Trend Rider: about 18% a year with drops around 22%
* Cycle Trader: about 33% a year with drops around 37%

With the AI, each 1% of drop you sit through earns roughly 0.9% a year. Holding BTC and ETH earned about 0.3%. That's about 3x more return for the same amount of pain.

**6. It's consistent no matter when you start.**  
BTC & ETH Cycle Trader beat holding from every one of 94 monthly start dates since 2018: good timing, bad timing, top of the market. Steady Trader never fell more than 6.3% below the money put in, from any start. Holding fell as far as 82.7% below it.

**7. Zero manual work.**  
That's 3 to 9 trades a week per portfolio, each with its own stop, all placed by the AI. I didn't place a single one.

**What it can't do:** over 8 years, holding had the higher typical yearly return in 4 of the 7 portfolios, because holding catches every bull run in full. But it also meant sitting through 71% to 88% drops without selling. Most people can't, and that's what AI is for. But this is only valid for investments that recover to a new high.

You can **watch the AI trade live** and track every move or use it on your own crypto coins. Just don't expect 20% a day. It does what's above, nothing more: [https://botsfolio.com/watch/botsfolio-ai](https://botsfolio.com/watch/botsfolio-ai)

comments.author: QuanTradin
comments.body: the week where every portfolio lost less than holding is the number I'd trust least, one down week mostly tells you the bots were partly in cash. how much of the 33% a year since 2018 was run live and how much is backtest?

replies.author: Mr_Hodlerr
replies.body:
You can check backtesting method here: [https://botsfolio.com/methodology/portfolios](https://botsfolio.com/methodology/portfolios)

Jan 1 2026 image I posted is live trading.

And yes that is the point, when to sell and keep in cash, how much to sell for cash and when to add to position and manage. Without rotating to cash you can't reduce drawdown in spot.

replies.author: QuanTradin
replies.body: so 2018 through 2025 is backtest and live only started in January, that's worth printing right next to the 33% on the chart. the cash rotation rule is where I'd push hardest: it sets the drawdown and it's also the easiest rule to fit to the past.

replies.author: Mr_Hodlerr
replies.body: 8 months of live trading across 400 coins with high volatility is enough to know you have a real edge, check the drops that happened during the live trading duration -63% to -40% and AI did -13% to -3%. So there is no fit here. When something survives cross assets, -63% drops in live trading it has a good edge.

replies.author: QuanTradin
replies.body: -13% against -63% is a real gap, no argument there. what I'd still separate out is that 400 coins mostly move with BTC, so it's closer to one test than 400, and 8 months is one regime. a stretch where alts bleed slowly instead of crashing is the one that would tell you more.

comments.author: DeskbotTrader
comments.body: The cash-exposure comparison would help separate timing skill from simply taking less risk: alongside buy-and-hold, could you show a fixed BTC/ETH-plus-cash benchmark with the same average market exposure as each portfolio? That would make the drawdown comparison much easier to interpret. Also, are the 94 start dates overlapping runs of one frozen model, or did each start date retrain using only information available then? Those test different things. Disclosure: this is the DeskBot maker account; we build a different trading tool, so I'm interested in clear evaluation rather than endorsing anyone's return figures.

comments.author: Shoddy_Peanut7320
comments.body: Showing that holding had the higher yearly return in 4 of the 7 portfolios, and that the main benefit is smaller drops, is the honest framing, and the live table next to the backtest table is a good setup. A few things I'd keep in mind when reading it. The 94 monthly starts overlap heavily, so "beat holding from every start" is closer to a handful of independent market cycles than 94 tests. The rules were presumably chosen while looking at the 2018 to 2026 data, so only the live period since January is out of sample, and that was a falling market where staying mostly in cash would have won anyway. It would help to publish how many versions were tried before these were picked, and the live results by month once the market is rising. Cymetica's Backtest Labs is one place to see how strategy results get compared against a benchmark.

replies.author: Mr_Hodlerr
replies.body: Well how did it know in live trading that the market is going down and hold in cash? 300 to 65 trades have been performed since live trading so it was not just in cash. For example Crypto cycle trader did 300 trades and ended up +27% vs +8% buy & hold. You can check the trade history of crypto cycle trader here: [https://botsfolio.com/crypto/watch/botsfolio-ai/portfolio/crypto-cycle-trader](https://botsfolio.com/crypto/watch/botsfolio-ai/portfolio/crypto-cycle-trader)

comments.author: Maleficent-Success-6
comments.body:
The live results are interesting, particularly the drawdown reduction, but I'd be careful about treating 400 coins as 400 independent confirmations of an edge.

Crypto assets share a lot of common market exposure. If most of them decline together, successfully reducing exposure during that period may represent one broadly shared regime decision rather than hundreds of independent successful predictions.

I'm building TIYlab, a non-custodial Bitcoin portfolio automation project, and separating genuine timing value from simply taking less market risk is something I'm particularly interested in.

I'd compare each portfolio against a simple BTC/ETH-and-cash benchmark with comparable exposure and costs, then examine whether the active timing decisions add value beyond that baseline.

I'd also separate the number of trades from the number of independent market conditions tested.

Eight months of live execution is useful evidence, but it doesn't necessarily establish how the strategy behaves across multiple independent bull and bear regimes.

Have you measured how much of the live outperformance remains after matching the benchmark's market exposure?
